items.t: BMO stock: Two investor conferences shape the week
sum: Bank of Montreal put investor events at the center of its week, with two conferences covering financial services and technology. The gatherings brought company leaders, investors and industry participants together in Florida and New York.

BMO Capital Markets held its inaugural Financials Conference in Boca Raton on November 9-10, 2026. In its official announcement, BMO said the agenda would address industry performance, growth opportunities, competitive dynamics, operational priorities and emerging trends.

The conference focused on asset and wealth management, insurance, business services and payments. BMO said more than 70 public and private companies were expected to participate, giving investors a broad view of financial-services activity.

On November 12, BMO hosted its inaugural Technology and Innovation Leaders Conference at the InterContinental Barclay Hotel in New York. The BMO announcement said more than 100 public and private companies were set to take part.

Discussion topics included artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, enterprise software, digital payments, semiconductors and quantum computing. For investors, the program linked BMO's capital-markets activity with technology themes that are reshaping financial services and corporate spending.

sum: Технологическая конференция Банка Монреаля приобрела новый взгляд на квантовую безопасность 13 ноября 2026 года после того, как SEALSQ рассказал о круглом столе, состоявшемся на мероприятии BMO Capital Markets в Нью-Йорке. Дискуссия добавляет новые детали к теме конференции и расширяет фокус внимания инвесторов за пределы традиционного банковского дела.

Согласно сообщению GlobeNewswire, опубликованному Yahoo Finance, генеральный директор SEALSQ Карлос Морейра присоединился к круглому столу по квантовой тематике на Конференции лидеров технологий и инноваций 12 ноября. Модератором сессии выступил аналитик BMO Capital Markets Харш Кумар, в котором также участвовали руководители Arqit Quantum и Quantum Computing Inc.

Обсуждение касалось коммерческого внедрения, безопасных полупроводников, фотонных квантовых вычислений и требований безопасности, связанных с искусственным интеллектом. SEALSQ также подчеркнул свое внимание к постквантовой криптографии, защите подключенных устройств и квантовой инфраструктуре.

Для BMO это мероприятие показывает, как ее платформа рынков капитала затрагивает технологические темы, выходящие за рамки ее основной банковской деятельности и деятельности по управлению активами. Новая информация о конференции актуальна для инвесторов, оценивающих широту исследований и институционального участия BMO, но не заменяет предстоящий отчет о прибылях банка в качестве основного теста операционной эффективности.

Bank of Montreal (BMO): Analysts Forecast 8% Upside as Strong Buy Technical Signal Supports Bullish Outlook
sum: (About StockTargetAdvisor.com (STA Research) is a Canadian investment research company specializing in advanced stock research and analysis).

The Bank of Montreal continues to be a strong Canadian banking investment opportunity, supported by improving operating performance, diversified North American banking operations, and strengthening technical momentum. Despite concerns surrounding Canada’s slowing economy, rising unemployment, elevated consumer debt and potential credit deterioration, BMO’s earnings recovery and strong capital position provide a constructive foundation for its longer-term investment outlook. The bank’s Canadian and U.S. operations, wealth management business and capital markets division offer diversified revenue streams, although its exposure to economically sensitive lending remains an important investment consideration.

Analyst sentiment remains positive according to the analyst consensus, which assigns BMO as a “Buy” rating and an average 12-month target price of C$265 per share. Based on the November 10 closing price of C$245.21, this forecast represents approximately 8.1% potential capital appreciation over the next 12 months. Desjardins Securities maintained its Hold recommendation on November 11 with a C$260 target, suggesting approximately 6.0% upside.

BMO’s third-quarter fiscal 2026 financial results demonstrated meaningful underlying earnings improvement. Adjusted net income increased 19% year over year to C$2.86 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to C$3.96. Adjusted return on equity improved to 14.0%, compared with 12.0% in the prior-year period. Provisions for credit losses declined to C$722 million from C$797 million, suggesting improving credit performance during the quarter. However, reported earnings remained below adjusted results, illustrating the importance of distinguishing recurring operating profitability from restructuring and other adjustments. The bank’s Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio of approximately 13% also provides a substantial capital buffer against potential economic deterioration.
From a valuation perspective, BMO trades at approximately 20 times trailing earnings and 15.3 times forward earnings, with a price-to-book ratio near 2.0 times.

Ottawa promises reform to spur competition in the banking sector
sum: Ottawa is promising legislative changes to boost competition in Canada’s banking sector in the federal budget released Thursday, aiming to make it easier for new financial institutions to enter the market and gain a foothold.

The government will change the law that governs Canada’s banking regulator, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, to add a “secondary competition objective” to its mandate, the budget says. The current OSFI mandate focuses solely on maintaining a stable and sound financial system.
Further amendments to the acts governing banks, trust companies and insurers will establish a one-year timeline for making decisions on applications to create new banks, the budget says.

OSFI superintendent Peter Routledge has already been keenly focused on bringing competition and innovation into Canada’s highly concentrated banking sector. Canada’s banking industry is dominated by the Big Six banks – Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto-Dominion Bank, Bank of Nova Scotia, Bank of Montreal, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and National Bank of Canada – that hold more than 90-per-cent market share.
In June, Mr. Routledge launched a pilot project that could strip years off the process to become a bank in a bid to bring more competitors into the market.

Over the next decade, OSFI will have to regulate through a period of immense change in the financial sector, Mr. Routledge said in an interview in October. “Canadians want more competition,” he said at the time.

Thursday’s budget also seeks to allow more flexible ownership structures for smaller banks, making it easier for them to grow larger in a market that is highly concentrated and dominated by Canada’s Big Six lenders.

items.t: Can Mulvihill Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) Maintain Its Distribution Momentum?
sum: - Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF declared a five-cent monthly distribution.
- Holdings centre on six major Canadian banks, with options used to add income.

Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) MBNK (TSX:MBNK) declared its monthly cash distribution in a release from Mulvihill Capital Management Inc. dated, setting the payment at five cents per share. The distribution is payable to shareholders of record, and it matches the amount shown in the manager's two previous monthly notices, which means the income stream has stayed level since the notices that preceded it. The announcement also offers a fresh read on sentiment toward exchange-traded funds across the TSX.

The steady payment is the main news in the announcement, but it also offers a chance to look at how this relatively new listing works. The fund launched on the Toronto Stock Exchange and is built around the common shares of six large Canadian banks, supplemented by an option-writing program intended to generate extra income.

According to the latest release, the record date falls and the payment follows about a week later. The preceding notice, issued, set the same five-cent amount for payment, and the notice before that, issued, did likewise for payment. A consistent cadence of five cents each month has therefore been declared across three consecutive announcements. These details form part of the latest disclosure from Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) MBNK (TSX:MBNK) .

The announcements do not describe the source of the cash. Distributions from a fund like this can combine dividends received from the underlying shares, option premiums and, in some cases, a return of capital. The composition affects how the amounts are taxed under Canada Revenue Agency rules, and the formal breakdown appears on the tax slips that are issued after period end rather than in the monthly notices.

The fund's launch release, issued, stated that the portfolio consists mainly of the common shares of six Canadian banks: Bank of Montreal, The Bank of Nova Scotia, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, National Bank of Canada, Royal Bank of Canada and The Toronto-Dominion Bank. Those institutions form the core of the Canadian financial system, and they are among the largest constituents of the S&P/TSX Composite Index.

BMO stock: Stonepeak completes CAD 14.5 billion finance sale
sum: Bank of Montreal stock remains in focus after BMO completed the sale of its Transportation Finance and Vendor Finance businesses to Stonepeak on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Stonepeak said the businesses will operate as Longview Capital Solutions, with customer relationships and service arrangements continuing during the transition.

At closing, BMO transferred approximately 75 percent, or CAD 11 billion, of an estimated CAD 14.5 billion combined loan and lease portfolio to Stonepeak. The remaining balances are expected to transfer in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, subject to customary conditions.

The transaction is expected to improve BMO's common equity Tier 1 ratio by approximately 23 basis points in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. BMO retains a 19.9 percent interest in the Stonepeak-managed entity, preserving participation in the businesses' future development.

Stonepeak said Longview will operate as an independent commercial equipment finance company. Customers will continue working with the same experienced teams and systems, while BMO provides transition services and continues servicing and originating current and future loans on Longview's behalf. The details were reported in Stonepeak's announcement.

Wednesday’s analyst upgrades and downgrades
sum: Inside the Market’s roundup of some of today’s key analyst actions

Dollarama Inc.’s (DOL-T) nearly 10 per cent share price decline on Tuesday in the wake of fourth quarter earnings was “overdone”, said Desjardins Securities analyst Chris Li, who said his long-term positive thesis remains intact.

Mr. Li was one of several analysts cutting his price target on Dollarama even as he was still recommending the stock as a buy. Investors punished the stock largely because of softer-than-expected fourth quarter same-store sales growth and heavier-than-expected losses in Australia. Yet analysts were largely willing to overlook those negatives to focus on what lies ahead.

“DOL reiterated that the 1.6% traffic decline reflected unfavourable weather rather than intensifying competition. Since the beginning of FY27, traffic has recovered as weather has normalized. Excluding calendar shifts and estimated weather effects, we estimate 4Q same-store sales growth [SSSG] at ~4% (at the high end of DOL’s long-term target). We believe 1Q-to-date SSSG is tracking above management’s 3–4% annual guide, supported by price increases in consumables in late FY26," Mr. Li said in a note to clients.

“Investors were also focused on heavier losses expected for Australia in FY27 as DOL enters the first full year of its multi-year transformation. We have increased our loss estimate to ~C$70m from C$24m. This includes A$35–45m of incremental integration expenses, with the remainder from lost sales due to the transition to lower-priced Dollarama items, store openings and reno costs etc. It is too early to know if FY27 is the peak year for losses for Australia. It will depend on how well consumers perceive the Dollarama products. Management’s confidence rests on the fact the products will offer the same compelling value proposition as Canada," he added.
Mr. Li cut his price target to C$205 from C$218 to reflect a more conservative near-term outlook, though that still leaves considerable upside for the next 12 months.
National Bank analyst Vishal Shreedhar cut his price target to C$198 from C$225 and reiterated an “outperform” rating, calling the fourth quarter results “satisfactory”.

items.t: RBC, CIBC, TD Bank, BMO, National Bank and Scotiabank: A breakdown of the big banks’ first-quarter earnings
sum: Canada’s biggest banks reported their first-quarter earnings this week, covering the three months that ended Jan. 31.

Bank of Nova Scotia kicked off the first-quarter earnings season on Tuesday, followed by Bank of Montreal and National Bank of Canada on Wednesday. Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto-Dominion Bank and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce closed out the week on Thursday.

All six banks posted higher profit that beat analysts’ estimates. Analysts broadly expected profits to rise in the first quarter as the lenders continue to shrug off concerns over the U.S. trade war, and provisions for credit losses – the money banks set aside to cover sour loans – to edge higher slightly.
Bank of Nova Scotia BNS-T reported first-quarter earnings that topped analysts’ estimates as profit rose across its businesses, shrugging off concerns of tepid loan growth and tariffs.

Scotiabank earned $2.29-billion, or $1.73 per share, in the three months that ended Jan. 31. That compared with $993-million, or $0.66 per share, in the same quarter last year, which included an impairment loss of $1.36-billion on the sale of banking operations in Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama.
Adjusted to exclude certain items, the bank said it earned $2.05 per share. That beat the $1.95 per share analysts expected, according to data from S&P Capital IQ.

In the quarter, Scotiabank set aside $1.18-billion in provisions for credit losses. That was slightly higher than the same quarter last year and included $73-million against loans that are still being repaid, based on models that use economic forecasting to predict future losses.
